x: We have already stated before what we have said about the meaning of <Ha Mim>, and the statement on this topic is like the statement on that.
And His statement:
h
A revelation from the Most Gracious
, the Most Merciful. God Almighty says: This Qur’an is
h
a revelation from the Most Gracious
, the Most Merciful. He sent it down to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
A Book whose verses are explained in detail. He says: A Book whose verses are explained in detail.

c: As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his statement:
h
His verses are detailed
, he said: His verses are made clear. And His saying:
h
An Arabic Qur’an
, God Almighty says: Its verses are explained in detail in this way. Arabic grammarians differed about the reason for the accusative case of the Qur’an.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said that his statement, A Book detailed means the Book is the predicate of a subject that states that the revelation is a Book. Then he said, Its verses were detailed,
h
an Arabic Qur’an

, making the verb preoccupied with the verses until it became like the subject, so he put the Qur’an in the accusative case. He said, A bearer of good tidings and a warner, as an adjective. If you wish, you can make it accusative for praise, as if when he mentioned it, he began to praise it, so he said, We mentioned
h
an Arabic Qur’an
, a bearer of good tidings and a warner, and We mentioned it as
h
an Arabic Qur’an
. What preceded in mentioning it was evidence of what was implied.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said, He put the Qur’an in the accusative case as a verb, meaning its verses were detailed in this way. He said, The accusative case may be for severance, because the speech is complete when he said, ‘His verses.’ He said: If it had been raised as an attribute of the Book, it would have been correct, as he said in another place: A blessed Book which We have revealed to you [p. 29]. And he said: Likewise, his saying:
h
A bearer of good tidings and a warner contains what is in an Arabic Qur’an
. And His statement:
h
For a people who know
means: The verses of this Book were explained in detail as
h
an Arabic Qur’an
h
for a people who know

the Arabic language, bringing them good tidings, giving them good tidings if they believe in it and act according to what was revealed in it of God’s limits and obligations, of Paradise. And as a warner: He says: And a warner of whoever denies it and does not act according to what is in it, of God’s command in this worldly life and of eternal damnation in the fire of Hell in the Hereafter.

And His statement: But most of them turned away means that God Almighty says: So they were too arrogant to listen to it and ponder the proofs of God in it, and most of these people to whom this Qur’an was sent down as a bearer of good tidings and a warner turned away from it, and they are the people of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So they do not listen means that they do not listen to it or hear it, out of turning away from it and being arrogant.
As a bringer of good tidings and a warner, but most of them turned away and did not hear.

God the Almighty says: “And these polytheists who turned away from the signs of God, from the polytheists of Quraysh, said when Muhammad, the Prophet of God, called them to acknowledge the Oneness of God and to believe in what is in this Quran of God’s commands and prohibitions, and all that was revealed therein, “
h
Our hearts are within coverings

” meaning: in coverings from that which you call to O Muhammad “of the Oneness of God and your belief in what you have brought to us. We do not understand what you say. “And in our ears is deafness” meaning heaviness, we do not hear what you call to out of the weight and aversion to what he calls to.” The meanings of these letters were explained before with their supporting evidence, and what the people of interpretation said about them was mentioned, so we disliked repeating that in this place.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
Our hearts are within coverings
, he said: They have coverings on them like quivers for arrows.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: And they said, ‘
h
Our hearts are within coverings
,’ he said: coverings over them, and in our ears is deafness, he said: deafness. And His saying:
h
And between us and you is a veil

. They say: And between us and you, O Muhammad, is a veil because of which we and you cannot meet, and we cannot see each other. And that veil is their difference in religion, because their religion was the worship of idols, and the religion of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him. And that is the veil that they claimed was between them and the Prophet of God, and that is their disagreement with each other in religion. And his saying: Then work, for we will work. He says: They said to him, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Then work, O Muhammad, according to your religion and what you say is the truth. We will work according to our religion and what we say is the truth. And leave our call to what you call us to of your religion, for we will call your call to our religion.” The word min was inserted in his statement:
h
And between us and you is a veil
, meaning:
h
And between us and you is a veil
, to emphasize the statement.

x: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to those of your people who turn away from the signs of God: O people, I am only a human being from the children of Adam, like you in kind, form and appearance. I am not an angel. It is revealed to me means: God reveals to me that you have no deity worthy of worship except One deity. So be upright towards Him means: So be upright towards Him in obedience, and direct your faces towards Him in desire and worship, not towards gods and idols. And seek His forgiveness means: And ask Him to pardon you for your past sins by repenting from your polytheism, and He will accept your repentance and forgive you.
And His statement:
h
And woe to the polytheists * Who do not give zakat and who

, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers. God Almighty says: And the pus of the people of Hell, and what flows from them, for those who claim to have a partner with God, worshipping idols instead of Him, who do not give zakat. The commentators differed on this.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: those who do not give God the obedience that purifies them and sanctifies their bodies, and do not believe in His Oneness. This is a statement attributed to Ibn Abbas.
The narration mentioned that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And woe to the polytheists * who do not give zakat
, he said: They are those who do not testify that there is no god but God.

c: Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, he said: Hafs told us, he said: Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: his statement:
h
And woe to the polytheists * who do not give zakat means those who do not say there is no god but God

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: those who do not acknowledge the zakat on their money that God has imposed on it, and do not give it to its people. We have also mentioned those who said this before.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And woe to the polytheists * Who do not give zakat. He said: They do not acknowledge it nor believe in it. It was said: Zakat is the bridge to Islam, whoever cuts it off will be saved, and whoever refrains from it will perish. The apostates after the Prophet of God said: As for the prayer, we pray, and as for the zakat, by God, do not seize our wealth. Abu Bakr said: By God, I do not separate between something that God has joined together, and by God, if they withhold from me even a rope from what God and His Messenger have enjoined, I will fight them over it.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
And woe to the polytheists * who do not give zakat

. He said: If they paid zakat while they were polytheists, it would not benefit them. The correct statement about this is what was said by those who said: Its meaning is: They do not pay zakat on their wealth. This is because this is the most well-known meaning of zakat, and His statement,
h
and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter

, is evidence that this is the case, because the disbelievers meant by this verse did not testify that there is no god but God. If His statement, those who do not pay zakat, meant those who do not testify that there is no god but God, His statement,
h
and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter
, would not have had any meaning, because it is known that whoever does not testify that there is no god but God does not believe in the Hereafter. In following God’s statement,
h
and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter
, His statement, those who do not pay zakat, indicates that zakat in this context refers to zakat on wealth. His statement:
h
And they are disbelievers in the Hereafter
, meaning: And they are disbelievers in the establishment of the Hour, and God will raise His creation alive from their graves after their affliction and destruction.

x: God Almighty says: “Indeed, those who believed in God and His Messenger, and did what God and His Messenger commanded them to do, and refrained from what We forbade them from - and that is the righteous deeds - will have a reward uninterrupted.” He says: For those who do that, there will be a reward undiminished from what He promised them to reward them for.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, and we have explained it previously in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
For them is a reward uninterrupted

x: Some of them said: Undiminished.
Some of them said: Uninterrupted.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: An unfailing reward means: undiminished.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, he said: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
For them is a reward uninterrupted
, he said: It is calculated.

x: And His saying: Indeed, you disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days, that is, Sunday and Monday. And this is what the reports came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the scholars said. We have mentioned much of this before, and we will mention some of what we did not mention before, God willing.
He mentioned some of the report that we did not mention before:

c: Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Baqqal, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas - Hannad
m: said: I read the rest of the hadith to Abu Bakr - “The Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about the creation of the heavens and the earth. He said: God created the earth on Sunday and Monday, and created the mountains on Tuesday and all the benefits in them, and created on Wednesday the trees, water, cities, built-up areas, and ruins. So these are four. Then he said: Do you disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and make rivals to Him?
h
That is the Lord of the worlds

. And He placed therein firm mountains above it and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask, for whoever asks. He said: And on Thursday He created the heaven, and on Friday He created the stars, the sun, the moon, and the angels, until three hours remained of it. In the first of these three hours He created the appointed time when whoever dies, and in the second He cast afflictions on everything that benefits people, and in the third He created Adam and settled him in Paradise, and He ordered Iblis to prostrate to him, and He expelled him from it in the last hour.” The Jews said, Then what then, O Muhammad? He said, Then He established Himself on the Throne. They said, You would have been right if you had completed it. They said, Then He rested. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, became extremely angry, so the verse was revealed, “And We created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us. So be patient over what they say.”
r
Tamim bin Al-Muntasir narrated to us:

c: Ishaq informed us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ghalib bin Ghallab, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: God created one day and named it Sunday. Then He created a second and named it Monday. Then He created a third and named it Tuesday. Then He created a fourth and named it Wednesday. Then He created a fifth and named it Thursday. He said: So He created the earth in two days, Sunday and Monday, and He created the mountains on Tuesday, and that is what the people say: It is a heavy day. He created the locations of the rivers and trees on Wednesday, and He created the birds, wild animals, vermin, and beasts on Thursday, and He created man on Friday, so He finished creating everything on Friday.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: He created the earth in two days on Sunday and Monday. And it has been said otherwise.

c: This is what Al-Qasim bin Bishr bin Maruf and Al-Hussein bin Ali told me.
m: They said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:

c: Ismail bin Umayya told me, on the authority of Ayoub bin Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’,
m: the freed slave of Umm Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took my hand and said: God created the soil on Saturday, and created the mountains in it on Sunday, and created the trees on Monday, and created the unpleasant things on Tuesday, and created the light on Wednesday, and spread the animals in it on Thursday, and created Adam after the afternoon prayer on Friday, the last creation in the last hour of the hours of Friday, between the afternoon prayer and the night.” His statement: And you attribute to Him rivals, meaning: And you attribute to the One Who created this way rivals, and they are equal men whom you obey in disobeying God. We have already explained the meaning of rivals with evidence previously. And His statement:
h
That is the Lord of the worlds

means: He who performed this action and created the earth in two days is the Owner of all the jinn and mankind, and all other kinds of creation, and everything below Him is owned by Him. So how can it be possible for Him to have a rival? And can a powerless slave who is unable to do anything be a rival to his Owner who is able to do it?

x: God Almighty says: And He placed on the earth which He created in two days firm mountains, which are the fixed ones on the earth above it, meaning: above the earth on its surface. His saying:
h
And blessed it
means: And He blessed the earth and made it always good for its people.
It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Saddī in this regard:

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And blessed it
he said: He caused its trees to grow.
h
And measured therein its sustenance
The interpreters differed on this.

x: Some of them said: He determined therein the sustenance of its people, meaning their provisions and livelihoods.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: h
And He has measured therein its sustenance
. He said: Its provisions.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God’s statement,
h
And measured therein its sustenance
, he said: He measured therein the provisions of the servants, the One with sustenance.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And He has measured therein its sustenance
, meaning: its sustenance for its people.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: He determined for it what would be suitable for it.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Da’laj, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He has measured therein its sustenance
, he said: its provision.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And He determined therein its mountains, rivers, and trees.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And He determined therein its sustenance: He created therein its mountains, rivers, seas, trees, and all its inhabitants from among the animals.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And He has measured therein its sustenance
. He said: Its mountains, its animals, its rivers, and its seas.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that its sustenance was determined from the rain.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And measured therein its sustenance
, he said: from the rain.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He determined in each town what He did not make in the other town, due to the livelihood of some of them from others through trade from town to town.
Who said that?

c: Al-Husayn bin Muhammad Al-Dhara’ told me, he said: Abu Muhsin told us, he said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And measured therein its sustenance
, he said: Al-Yamani is in Yemen, and Al-Sabari is in Sabur.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me, he said: Abu Muhsin told us on the authority of Hisin, he said:
m: Ikrimah said, And He measured therein its sustenance, the Yamaniyyah in Yemen, and the Sabiriyah in Sabur, and similar things.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said:
m: I heard Hisin on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement:
h
And He has measured therein its sustenance
, he said: In every land there is sustenance that is not suitable in any other land, the Yemeni in Yemen, and the Sabari in Sabur.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Husayn told us on the authority of Ikrimah
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He has measured therein its sustenance
, he said: The land in which there is

x: And His statement:
h
Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth

, ‘Come, willingly or by compulsion.’ They said, ‘We come willingly.’ Meaning, the Most High, mentioned: Then He directed Himself to the heaven, then ascended to the heaven. We have already explained the statements of the scholars on this matter previously. And His saying:
h
And He said to it and to the earth

, ‘Come, willingly or by compulsion,’ God Almighty says: God said to the heaven and the earth, “Bring what I have created in you. As for you, O heaven, bring forth what I have created in you of the sun, the moon, and the stars. As for you, O earth, bring forth what I have created in you of trees, fruits, and plants, and split open the rivers.” They said, We have come willingly, “We have come with what You have created in us of Your creation, and responding to Your command, we do not disobey Your command.”
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Hisham told us: Ibn Yaman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Then He said to it and to the earth, ‘Come, willingly or by compulsion.’ They said, ‘We come willingly.’ He said: God said to the heavens: ‘Bring forth My sun and moon, and bring forth My stars.’ And He said to the earth: ‘Spread forth your rivers and bring forth your fruits.’ They said: ‘Give us willingly.’”

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Sulayman al-Ahwal, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement, Bring: give. And regarding His statement, They said, ‘We have come’: they said, ‘We have given.’ And it was said: We came willingly, and He did not say obediently. The heaven and the earth are feminine, because the nun and the alif that are a metaphor for their names in His statement,
h
We have come are similar to the metaphor for the names of the male informants about themselves
, so He made His statement, obediently, follow the same pattern as the information about men.

x: Some of the Arab scholars used to say: He took him to the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them.
Others among them said: It was said thus because when they spoke, they resembled the males of the sons of Adam.
God Almighty says: He completed the creation of seven heavens in two days, which were Thursday and Friday.

c: Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke from the breathing of water when it breathed, and He made it one heaven, then He split it apart, and He made them seven heavens in two days, Thursday and Friday. And it was called Friday because on it He gathered together the creation of the heavens and the earth. His saying:
h
And He revealed to each heaven its command
, meaning: And He cast into each of the seven heavens what He wanted of creation. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
And He revealed to each heaven its command
, he said: What God commanded and willed.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: And He revealed in each heaven its command. He said: He created in each heaven its creation of angels and the creation in it of seas and mountains of hail, and what is not known.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And He revealed in each heaven its command, meaning He created something in it, its sun, its moon, its stars, and its goodness. And His statement:
h
And We have adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as protection
. God Almighty says: And We have adorned the lowest heaven for you, O people, with the stars, which are the lamps.

c: As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps. He said: Then He adorned the heaven with stars, making them an adornment and a protection from the devils. The Arabists differed about the reason for placing the word in the accusative case in his statement: and preservation.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is in the accusative case in the sense of: And We preserved it with preservation, as if he had said: And We preserve it with preservation, because when he said: We adorned it with lamps, he had informed that he had looked into its matter and looked after it, so this indicates preservation, as if he had said: And We preserved it with preservation.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is in the accusative case in the sense of: And We adorned it with preservation, because if the waw had been dropped, it would have been: Indeed, We adorned the lowest heaven with preservation. This second statement is closer to the truth in our view than the first. We have explained the reason for this in a similar place in more than one place in this book, so there is no need to repeat it. And His statement:
h
That is the decree of the Almighty

, the All-Knowing, God Almighty says: This that I have described to you of My creation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them, and My adornment of the lowest heaven with the adornment of the stars, as I have explained, is the decree of the Almighty in His punishment of His enemies, the All-Knowing of the secrets and open secrets of His servants, and their management according to what is best for them.

God Almighty says: If these polytheists turn away from this argument that you, O Muhammad, explain to them, and you alert them to it, and they do not believe in it and do not acknowledge that the one who does that is God, besides whom there is no god, then say to them: I have warned you, O people, of a thunderbolt that will destroy you like the thunderbolt of Aad and Thamud. We have previously explained that the meaning of thunderbolt is: everything that spoils something and changes its state. It has been said in this context that it refers to a calamity and punishment from God.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ‘Aad and Thamud
, he said: He says: I have warned you of a calamity like the calamity of ‘Aad and Thamud. He said: A punishment like the punishment of ‘Aad and Thamud.

x: And His statement:
h
When there came to them the messengers from before them and from behind them

means: Say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud that destroyed them, when the messengers came to 'Ad and Thamud from before them, so His statement: <when>is a connection to thunderbolt. And what He meant by His statement: from before them are the messengers that came to the fathers of those who were destroyed by the thunderbolt from these two nations. And what He meant by His statement: and from behind them is from behind the messengers who were sent to their fathers as messengers to them. That is because God sent Hud to 'Ad, but they denied him after messengers who had preceded him to their fathers as well, so they denied them, and so they were destroyed. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: If they turn away... to his statement: and those behind them, he said: The messengers who were before Hud, and the messengers who were after him. God sent messengers before him, and sent messengers after him. And His statement:
h
That you worship none but God

means, the Most High said: The messengers came to them with the order that they should worship none but God alone, with no partner for Him. They said: If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels means, the Most High said: So they said to their messengers when they called them to acknowledge the oneness of God: If our Lord had willed that we worship Him alone and not worship anything besides Him, He would have sent down to us angels from the heaven as messengers with what you call us to. He would not have sent you, even though you are human beings like us, but He was pleased with our worshipping what we worship, and for that reason He did not send angels to us to forbid us from that. And His statement:
h
Then we are disbelievers in that with which you have been sent
. He says: They said to their messengers: Then we are disbelievers in that with which your Lord has sent you to us, not believing in it.

x: God Almighty says: “As for ‘Aad, the people of Hud, they were arrogant towards their Lord and acted tyrannically in the land, arrogantly and insolently, without permission from God, and they said, ‘Who is stronger than us in strength?’ Did they not see that God, who created them and gave them what He gave them of great creation and great power, was stronger than them in strength, so they would fear His punishment and guard against His wrath, because of their disbelief in Him and their denial of His messengers. And they used to deny Our signs.” He says: And they used to deny Our proofs and arguments against them.
God Almighty says: Then We sent upon the people of Aad a furious wind. The commentators differed on the meaning of as-sarar.
Some of them said: It means a strong wind.
Mention of those who said that:

He destroyed you
is in the accusative case, meaning:
h
He destroyed you
. It may also be possible that it is in the nominative case by resumption, meaning:
h
He destroyed you

(Luqman 31:2-3)

in the reading of those who read it in the nominative case. The meaning of the statement is: This assumption that you assumed about your Lord, that He does not know much of what you do, is what destroyed you, because because of this assumption you dared to transgress the prohibitions of God and committed them, and did what God forbade you from, so that destroyed you and ruined you. So you have become among the losers. He says: So today you have become among the ruined, and you have been deceived by selling your homes in Paradise for the homes of the people of Paradise in Hell.
